feature: Blender-style editor tools and move gizmo

seams.what: the viewport currently has no header, left tool shelf, transform context, or status bar
seams.evidence: the current section begins directly with the canvas and overlays; Blender-style tool placement must enter here to stay spatially attached to the view
seams.asks: which viewport chrome should be persistent, and which panels should collapse on smaller screens?

seams.what: run, point, edit, cadence, and rollback are currently mixed into one wrapping bottom strip
seams.evidence: the closest existing feature placed all editor actions here; the redesign must decide what moves into viewport tools versus remains global
seams.asks: should the old strip disappear entirely, or retain run and cadence while object tools move to the viewport?

seams.what: the two-column viewport/sidebar and bottom controls geometry controls every editor surface
seams.evidence: desktop uses a fixed 340px sidebar and mobile becomes a long vertical stack; Blender-like chrome requires a different spatial hierarchy in both widths
seams.asks: on narrow screens, should properties and conversation become drawers, bottom sheets, or remain stacked?

seams.what: the viewport surface owns the positioning context for floating editor chrome
seams.evidence: all new header, shelf, properties and status surfaces must layer over or around this positioned panel without reducing canvas usability
seams.asks: should tools overlay the canvas like Blender, or consume fixed rows and columns around it?

seams.what: the only reachable move interaction reads three absolute numeric fields and sends immediately
seams.evidence: a gizmo needs to coexist with precise numeric entry and share one commit/error path
seams.asks: should numeric entry remain visible alongside the arrows, move into a contextual properties panel, or be removed?

seams.anchor: export function dragToTranslation(from, axis, delta, snap = DEFAULT_SNAP_M) {
seams.what: axis-constrained destination snapping already exists but has no screen projection or arrow hit testing
seams.evidence: the closest point-and-edit feature deliberately left draggable arrows as a known gap while preserving the arithmetic needed by them
seams.asks: should dragging preview continuously and send once on release, and how should cancellation and snapping feel?

seams.what: point-mode drag currently owns pointer gestures for lasso selection while the renderer owns orbit outside point mode
seams.evidence: gizmo dragging must take capture before either lasso or orbit and release or cancel without changing selection
seams.asks: should Move be its own tool mode, and which mouse, keyboard, and touch gestures switch or constrain axes?

seams.what: the software renderer draws geometry and selection feedback but no transform manipulator
seams.evidence: a post-raster screen overlay can render labelled arrows without corrupting the depth-tested object-id picking channel
seams.asks: should arrows always render over geometry, fade when occluded, and use familiar X/Y/Z colours despite the one-accent design system?

seams.what: the renderer currently applies only authoritative transforms from viewport state
seams.evidence: smooth dragging needs a reversible local preview while the backend remains authoritative after pointer release or error
seams.asks: should the selected part move live under the cursor, or should only the gizmo preview until the server confirms?

seams.what: server transform updates are the authoritative result after an operator edit
seams.evidence: an optimistic preview must converge on this update and roll back visibly when an ERROR arrives instead
seams.asks: what feedback should appear while saving, on success, and when the move is rejected?

seams.what: all renderer colours must come from generated tokens, while the current system intentionally permits only one chromatic accent
seams.evidence: Blender-style X/Y/Z recognition normally depends on red, green, and blue; that needs an explicit exception or a labelled monochrome alternative
seams.asks: should the gizmo use familiar RGB axes, labelled single-accent arrows, or a hybrid?

seams.what: every new pure gizmo test file must be imported by the Windows test entry point
seams.evidence: frontend/CLAUDE.md documents that an unregistered sibling test silently disappears from npm run test:frontend
seams.asks: none — this is mechanical wiring required for any new gizmo-math module

seams.anchor: test('point mode visibly highlights hover and keeps a clicked part selected', async () => {
seams.what: the closest real-browser journey proves selection pixels but not editor-tool reachability or manipulation
seams.evidence: only a real canvas test can prove arrow hit targets, pointer capture, live preview, commit, cancellation, focus order, and responsive layout
seams.asks: which pointer, keyboard, touch, and narrow-screen paths are required for the first release?

seams.what: manual move operations already travel through annotation to the orchestrator and scene history
seams.evidence: the gizmo can send the existing absolute move_object payload once per committed drag without widening the wire protocol
seams.asks: should one final move be sent on release, or should intermediate moves also enter undo history?

seams.what: the previous feature record explicitly names draggable viewport arrows as unfinished
seams.evidence: closing the documented gap should point future maintainers to the new interaction and its constraints
seams.asks: should this release also expose rotate and scale tools, or place them visibly as disabled/future tools?
